html:
The Anguthimri were an Aboriginal Australian people of the west coast of Cape York Peninsula, from the Mission River north to the Pennefather River and west to Duyfken Point. Their language is now extinct.

In 1606 the Dutch ship Duyfken under Willem Janszoon reached this coast, the first recorded European landing in Australia. The crew clashed with local people near the Pennefather River.

Their neighbours were the Mpalitjanh, Luthigh and Awngthim. A Presbyterian mission opened at Mapoon in 1891. From the 1960s bauxite mining at Weipa took over much of the coast, and in 1963 the Mapoon people were forcibly moved away.
